public_rationale: On the contextual reading, continued scaling was an evidence-backed extrapolation. Early research measured empirical relationships, and subsequent work tested predictions while retaining explicit assumptions and limitations. The claim is supported as a statement about indefinite continuation. It would be misleading if read as saying that scaling gains themselves were never demonstrated.
limitations: Hypothesis does not mean unsupported speculation.
The cited papers establish the methodological status of influential scaling research, not an exhaustive history of every scaling argument.
This assessment does not establish that scaling had stopped working.

our_interpretation: The target is the historical status of continued scaling through 2024-11-10. No starting date is supplied.

evidence.explanation: Early scaling research built its claims from empirical measurements across several tasks. This supports the distinction between observed regularities and guarantees about their indefinite continuation.

The authors explicitly qualify their scaling predictions and identify assumptions about their fitted relationships. Their successful Chinchilla experiment also shows that hypothesis should not be read as an unsupported guess.
